abbreviations.description: List of abbreviation rules for pktstat. Each item is a map with 'abbrev' and 'pattern'. If 'abbrev' is omitted or empty, the pattern text itself is used as the abbreviation name. See pktstat(1) Abbreviations section for format: [abbrev@]pattern. The pattern supports '*' wildcard for non-space characters and spaces for whitespace matching. Lines starting with # or blank lines are ignored by pktstat but here we only emit valid entries. Items structure: abbrev (string, optional, defaults to pattern text if empty), pattern (string, required). The 'default' value for 'abbrev' inside an item should be None or omitted to let pktstat use the pattern text, but since schema requires a default, we use an empty string which implies 'use pattern text'. However, to strictly match 'default' as a bare scalar, we define the item schema such that 'abbrev' defaults to the pattern? No, Jinja2 default filter handles this. The values_schema for the list item must be flat. Let's define 'abbrev' as a string with default '' and 'pattern' as a string. The template uses {{ item.abbrev | default('*') }}? No, the man page says 'If the optional abbrev is not specified, the pattern text itself is used'. So if abbrev is empty, we output just the pattern. If abbrev is set, we output 'abbrev @ pattern'. Let's adjust template logic: {% if item.abbrev %}{{ item.abbrev }} @ {{ item.pattern }}{% else %}{{ item.pattern }}{% endif %}. This is allowed. The item schema: abbrev: {type: string, default: '', description: 'The abbreviation name. If empty, pattern is used as name.'}, pattern: {type: string, description: 'The pattern to match.'}. Wait, the prompt says 'default' MUST be a bare scalar. '' is a bare scalar. But for the list, the default is []. For the items, I need to specify the schema of the items. The prompt says: 'For a list-of-objects, add items as a FLAT map field-name -> {type, default, description}'. So I will define `abbreviations.items.abbrev` and `abbreviations.items.pattern`.
